# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been on the shelf since the Clinton administration. Marisol Reyes found it while shelving returns: a pencilled note in the margin of page 212, beside a sentence about the Yorkshire moors. *Moorland doesn't bloom in January,* the note read, in small, precise handwriting. *Heath would be more accurate.*

Marisol frowned. Patrons weren't supposed to write in library books, even in pencil, and certainly not in pencil so faint you'd miss it unless the light caught the page. She erased the note, or tried to. The graphite had pressed hard enough to leave a groove. She shelved the book and forgot about it.

Then came the note in *Moby-Dick*—*Sperm whales can't see well directly ahead; Ahab would know this*—and the one in a field guide to Pacific shorebirds, correcting a range map. *Marbled godwits winter as far south as Panama,* the handwriting said. *This map cuts them off at Mexico. Lazy.*

That one made Marisol laugh out loud, alone in the stacks at 4:45 on a Tuesday,
